reading: Partial: all 40 readings with three inputs, 16 of 40 with four inputs, none with five. The cells with four inputs are incomplete and the order in which readings were lost is not random (later readings are harder ones), so nothing is concluded about four or five inputs.

Three inputs: 7 laws reported in 40 readings (3, 3, 1 and 0 at noise 1, 5, 10 and 20 %), none inaccurate. None of the 7 is the law itself by the benchmark's test of form; all 7 are accurate on rows the reading never saw.
Four inputs: no law reported in 16 readings.

So far the reading says less as conditions widen, and what it did report was accurate. Seven reports are too few to bound the share of wrong reports: under the rule named on 25 November (apedp_dyn/discovery_l2/report_share.py) this is 'not shown'.

what: development, and PARTIAL: the product's table reading beyond its measured conditions, second run. Every shard stopped for ever part-way and ended at its time limit; 56 of 120 readings were written. Not a result, and not the measurement that was planned

what_stopped_it.not_the_cause: slowness: a reading took 164 to 372 s (median 237), so 30 readings fit in about two hours of the five allowed
what_stopped_it.reading: From about the tenth reading of a shard on, one search of the four had not answered by the searches' deadline in reading after reading (each signal comes about 105 s after the searches start: the 90 s budget and its grace). The portfolio then tells that process to stop; Julia handles the signal itself, prints 'signal 15: Terminated', and in 4 of 19 cases never exits. The portfolio waits for it for ever. Members that leave hard do not help here: the process is stopped before it reaches Python's exit hooks. hard_exit.BoundedPortfolio (2026-11-25) bounds the wait from outside; run 3 of this workflow uses it.
